This is the ADR-032 Tier-3 parse shape in full — sentinel probe, value assertions, construct an owned type — on provider-authored LLM tool calls. The default is the module-private sentinel `_MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD = object()`, NOT a usable value, and it is consumed IMMEDIATELY and explicitly: `if call_id is _MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD: raise AuditIntegrityError(...)`. Nothing is hidden — a missing field is a hard audit-integrity failure, as are a non-`str`, blank, oversized, or duplicate id, and the surviving value is snapshotted once into the frozen owned `_AdmittedToolCall`/`_AdmittedToolFunction` so nothing downstream can re-resolve it. A `runtime_checkable` Protocol `isinstance` is the forbidden alternative here, not the safer one: the function's docstring records elspeth-9ea866438b, where it rejected every genuine tool call from every provider because since Python 3.12 protocol member resolution uses `inspect.getattr_static`, which bypasses `__getattr__` — and LiteLLM's `ChatCompletionMessageToolCall` resolves `id`/`type`/`function` only through `BaseModel.__getattr__`. `getattr` also absorbs ONLY `AttributeError`; any other exception from a provider `__getattr__` propagates rather than being relabelled.

R2 `function = getattr(tool_call, "function", _MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD)`. Same ADR-032 sentinel-probe boundary on the same Tier-3 provider tool call. The sentinel is consumed transitively and totally: when `function` is `_MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD`, the two probes on the following lines find no `name`/`arguments` on a bare `object()` and yield the sentinel in turn, so `type(function_name) is not str or type(function_arguments) is not str` is True and the batch is refused with `AuditIntegrityError('Composer tool batch contains malformed provider function metadata')`. There is no path on which a missing `function` reaches dispatch. The probe cannot be a Protocol `isinstance` for the elspeth-9ea866438b reason recorded in the function docstring, and the read-once copy into the frozen `_AdmittedToolFunction` is what makes the snapshot authoritative.

R2 `function_name = getattr(function, "name", _MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD)`. Same ADR-032 sentinel-probe boundary on Tier-3 provider tool-call metadata. The sentinel is consumed by the exact-type assertion two lines down — `type(function_name) is not str` is True for `object()`, so an absent name and a non-string name are both refused with the same `AuditIntegrityError` and the batch never dispatches. The exact-type test is deliberate (a `str` subclass is not admitted into the frozen owned type), and the `getattr` probe rather than a Protocol check is required by elspeth-9ea866438b as recorded in the function docstring: real provider tool calls resolve this attribute through `BaseModel.__getattr__`, which `inspect.getattr_static` — and therefore a runtime_checkable Protocol — cannot see.

R2 `function_arguments = getattr(function, "arguments", _MISSING_TOOL_CALL_FIELD)`. Same ADR-032 sentinel-probe boundary, on the field carrying the raw untrusted JSON argument text. The sentinel is consumed by the same exact-type assertion as `function_name` (`type(function_arguments) is not str` -> `AuditIntegrityError`), so a provider object missing `arguments` is refused before the first await and before any side effect, rather than reaching `json.loads` as a sentinel. The value is snapshotted once into the frozen `_AdmittedToolFunction`, so the string that is parsed downstream is provably the string that was admitted here — the property the whole admit-before-dispatch boundary exists to give the audit trail. Protocol-based probing is excluded for the elspeth-9ea866438b reason recorded in the function docstring.
